title: Give no-write redaction and validation refusals on the host wire a distinct error code instead of storage_error
outcome: TermAl can tell a definitive no-write refusal (for example a secret-bearing turn_checkpoint argument) from a real storage failure, and stops replaying it
acceptance: On the host wire, StoreError::RedactionRefused answers with a distinct documented code (not storage_error); any other refusal that provably happens before any write is either given a distinct code under the same rule or listed as deliberately left as storage_error, with the reason
A test drives a turn_checkpoint carrying a secret-bearing argument through the host server and asserts the distinct code and that nothing was written (store unchanged)
The host protocol documentation lists the new code(s) as definitive no-write refusals, and TermAl is told the exact code(s) for its default-closed allowlist
